messages:
elaine: FYI ap-southeast GPU pool is hitting sustained 95% utilization for the last 20m. Error spike in the edge-serve stacks, 5xxs from slow OOMs. Thinking we should try a different admission tack for this region: 'patient hedging' — allow a tiny soft-queue window + hedged routing to nearby region before hard rejects. Thoughts?

mike: Can you paste the dashboard snapshot? what's the error breakdown — rejects vs timeouts vs slowpath latency?

elaine: Quick numbers: total qps 1800 -> capacity ~1900 but concurrent token-backed mem pressure causing slowpath for medium-length chats. 5xxs rose from 0.2% -> 1.9%. Rejects (hard) currently ~300/min due to admit controller. Timeouts ~40/min. Attached graf: https://grafana/reports/ap-southeast/1746 (looks like prefix cache churn)

raj: patient hedging sounds promising. My worry: increased tail latency for tiered customers and higher GPU-hours if we keep retrying across regions. Need cost guardrails.

elaine: Agreed. Proposal sketch:
- accept request into a tiny soft-queue (100ms token window) where we try to find local slot
- if >100ms, simultaneously issue a hedged request to a warm remote pool (sg/au) with abort-on-first-success
- if both slow, fallback to fast-reject with short retry-hint header (Retry-After: 2s)
- surface admission_decision header for observability (local_softqueued | hedged | reject)
- circuit-breaker: if remote hedging impact > X% of capacity increase, disable hedging automatically

sophia: How do we avoid thundering-herd to remote when soft-queue drains? Need pre-warm tokens or tokenized budget per customer. Also how to ensure fairness across priority tiers?

elaine: Implementation notes: we can integrate with existing admit controller. Pseudoconfig: 
```
admission_policy: {
  type: "patient_hedge",
  soft_queue_ms: 100,
  hedged_regions: ["ap-southeast-2"],
  remote_timeout_ms: 500,
  remote_budget_pct: 7
}
```
Budget enforced per-account and global. Priority tiers skip hedging or have smaller soft_queue_ms.

mike: This needs experiment gating. Suggest A/B: 5% production traffic in ap-southeast to start; monitor unit-cost, p95 latency, and error-rate. Add metric: hedged_success_rate and remote_gpu_credit_used.

raj: Also track correctness/regression: for chat streams we might get duplicate tokens if not careful with abort semantics. Ensure idempotency keys in transport + server-side dedup window.

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary group "patient-hedge-v1" created. Staging test with 1k synthetic chat sessions queued. CI: pass -> canary deploy 5% -> metrics alert rule quotas added.

elaine: Rollout steps I propose: 1) feature gate behind org-level flag, 2) run canary on low-priority customers, 3) collect hedged_success_rate, remote_cost_delta, p95_local_latency for 48h, 4) if remote_cost_delta < 12% and errors drop, expand to 25%.

sophia: Add SLA safety: for enterprise-tier customers keep hard-reject threshold lower (no hedging) unless customer opts in. Put doc note in runbook.

mike: One more: add quick cancel window instrumentation to measure how often local wins vs remote. If remote wins > 60% we might be misrouting; adjust locality rules.

elaine: Great. I'll open a PR with admit controller changes + config + runbook and link here. Can someone pair on the canary dashboard? @mike?

mike: I can pair. Setting up alarm groups and the cost dashboard now. Will post links when ready. :thumbsup:

elaine: Thanks — will file the PR and tag reviewers. If we see anything odd during the canary ping this thread.
